Brownfield renewal · give an industrial place a second life

Review closed or working industrial premises, compensate their recorded owners and displaced workers, pay for ground works, then fund housing, a local shop or green space. Existing industrial neighbours still affect rents and residential suitability. Renewing this site retires its former industrial location; reopening those jobs requires another lawful site.

Ground-work estimates and conditions

Ground preparation is priced from recorded enterprise age and footprint. Funded external crews require open regional trade and road access. Paid surveys/contracts are non-refundable; cancelling a review spends nothing.

How neighbourhoods evolve & land assembly works

Districts form from actual homes, jobs, active retail and road-accessible catchments. Market and employment patterns can overlap in a mixed-use block. Financial districts require real deposits or active loans plus at least one post-founding bank entrant; the three founding institutions alone are shown as a banking node. A new character must persist for 90 days; an emptied district dissolves after 180 days. Income bands compare observed after-tax income per resident with the town median; they do not assign identities or change wages. Property condition and funded service reach are shown separately.

Banks currently share townwide deposit and loan markets; the simulation does not assign branch-specific staff or customer service areas, so it cannot truthfully quote a privately built branch as expanding access. Plans govern construction, preserving existing titles.

Land assembly pays the recorded owner, relocates tenants to actual connected vacant homes, and compensates displaced workers. Paid cargo and construction must settle first. After clearance, select and fund the new service through Public Works.

Investors respond to demand automatically. Road developers finance extensions from regional capital; housing developers choose lots near jobs, and merchants enter underserved markets. Underground investors evaluate population and density, then fund stations and tunnels. Farmers acquire field plots and raise grain output; factory owners and freight depots respond to supply and demand; landlords may replace cottages with apartments or towers after assembling a site; and airport investors require a major regional market, a clear runway, and long-term operating capital. SIMULATION PRINCIPLES

The economy runs as real linked accounts: wages and purchases move money among firms, families, the town treasury and the external region. Goods have inventory; people have jobs; firms have expenses. Government services spend actual cash and provide observable benefits.

Important: This is an experimental, self-contained Android adaptation. Policy coefficients are designed for gameplay, not calibrated forecasts of real municipal outcomes. Retain a text backup if you change devices or uninstall.
